description: String.codepoints(<<"a", 255, "b">>) is ["a", <<255, 98>>] in fz (measured on bea9d1ae5) and ["a", <<255>>, "b"] in Elixir 1.19.4. lib/string.fz codepoint_size(first_byte(s)) trusts the lead byte: 255 claims four bytes. It feeds next_codepoint (:651) and the walkers at :973, :1000 and :1021. Elixir treats a byte that does not start a valid UTF-8 sequence, or a truncated sequence, as a one-byte codepoint. Graphemes already get this rule from fz-sc8.23 (fz_grapheme_size). The distiller reads valid UTF-8 only.
title: An invalid byte is its own codepoint, as in Elixir
